title: observability: automate Prometheus/Grafana/log-shipping for Private installs; add upgrade/rollback hooks
author: Aisha Patel
description: Automate the observability stack provisioning and configuration for Private installs (VPC and on-prem) as part of the private-installer / helm / terraform workflows. Motivation: customers deploying Redwood Private frequently request a repeatable observability install path that matches hosted defaults (Prometheus, Grafana, node-exporter metrics, Fluent Bit/EFK log shipping) and integrates with our upgrade/rollback tooling. This PR adds a single helm umbrella chart (redwood-observability) with opinionated defaults, Terraform modules to provision required cloud resources and IAM roles for managed Private installs, installer hooks to run pre/post-upgrade migrations for dashboards and alerting rules, and idempotent log-shipping manifests for air-gapped environments. Changeset overview: - Helm: new chart under redwood-private-installer/helm/redwood-observability with subcharts for prometheus-operator, grafana (dashboards as configmaps), fluent-bit, and node-exporter. Charts expose values to toggle managed vs external deployments and to set storageClass/securityContext for on-prem. - Terraform: new modules in redwood-private-installer/terraform/observability to create S3 buckets for remote-write retention, create KMS keys and IAM bindings for metrics/logs, and optional managed Grafana workspace integration. - Installer: hooks added to installer/templates/hooks to apply dashboards and alerting rules before traffic switch; migrations are idempotent and use label-based reconciliation. - Upgrade/Rollback: added tests and scripts to gracefully migrate PrometheusRule names and preserve silence/alertmanager config during rollbacks; added a dry-run mode. - Docs and quickstart: new private-installs observability quickstart with example values for VPC and on-prem, and troubleshooting notes for common metrics mismatches. Testing: manual validation on a full VPC Private deployment in staging (k8s 1.25), unit tests for terraform modules (terratest snippets), helm lint + kubeval, and e2e smoke using perf-canary to ensure scraping and dashboard ingestion under load. Backwards compatibility: default values keep observability disabled to avoid impacting existing installs; we provide migration notes and a toggle for operators. Related Linear tickets: ENG-7245, ENG-7310. This PR is intended to be merged via squash once approvals and CI pass.
commits: init: add redwood-observability umbrella chart and subcharts (prometheus, grafana, fluent-bit)
feat(terraform): add observability modules (s3, kms, iam, grafana workspace)
chore(installer): add pre/post-upgrade hooks for dashboards and rules reconciliation
fix(helm): allow storageClass override and securityContext for on-prem nodes
test: add terratest snippets and e2e smoke for observability
docs: add private-installs observability quickstart and migration notes
review_comments: Miguel Santos (reviewer): Can we make the Grafana dashboards configurable as CRDs instead of configmaps to allow live updates? Suggestion: consider including a toggle and document tradeoffs.
Author (Aisha): Grafana CRD operators vary across distros; configmaps are more portable for now. Added a values.toggle grafana.useCRD and documented tradeoffs in quickstart.
Elena Park (reviewer): Terraform: need stricter IAM policy scoping for KMS/S3 resources and tests that simulate cross-account installs.
Author: Scoped down the IAM policies and added terratest cross-account snippets to tests directory. CI should catch policy regressions.
Jonah Kim (SRE): Will alerts fire during upgrade and cause noise? Need to silence alertmanager during migration window.
Author: Added optional installer hook to inject temporary silence with a configurable TTL; documented in quickstart and added to hooks.
release_notes: Add automated observability provisioning for Private installs: helm umbrella chart for Prometheus/Grafana/Fluent Bit; Terraform modules for cloud resources; installer pre/post-upgrade hooks for dashboards and alert rules; optional managed Grafana integration; dry-run upgrade mode; observability disabled by default to preserve existing installs.
